new_assertions.body: Stone-count parity is exactly the low bit of column-height XOR: p=X_h&1; the pair (X_h,p) carries no more information than X_h alone.
X_h and p are not Q-F, Q-A or Q-V sufficient on any of the five complete bounded controls, so the prior shortcut cannot be promoted as a standalone rank-sufficient value coordinate.
Because all 836 old transition ambiguities occur at fixed full support, no support-only invariant can resolve those representation splits.
X_h and p are invariants of the full column-permutation action but are constant on each orbit; they cannot explain or select the q_Sigma canonical representative.
The final-board-mover and sole-open-column ownership formulas eliminate current p entirely; their primitive explanation is persistent geometry plus row/open-column structure, not height XOR.
Frontier blocking requires mover residual information not recoverable from support-only descriptors, so the irreducible Q-F kernel has a residual-semantic component independent of support algebra.
R/G/H are each pointwise contained in exact single-residual feasibility E1 over all tested cases, but E1 and RGH are not generally the same partition.
F∘E1 and RFGH induce exactly the same state partition on all five complete tested domains despite differing normalized residual representatives in some cases.

The tested safe-forgetting family is more compactly described at quotient level as frontier reduction composed with single-residual ownership feasibility, with R/G/H providing one rank-local recoding of that quotient in the tested domains.
